subject: gptme
title: Three-tier compaction: rule-based 3-phase trim, LLM summarize fallback, and lossless-view retry on provider overflow
one_why: Nuance vs cline-1/codex-3/pi-2: the tiers share one budget trigger and hand off on estimated savings (>=10% rule-based else summarize), and the third tier is retry-after-compact with a shrink-monotonicity guard (chat.py:865) that refuses a retry whose provider input did not actually shrink.

subject: gptme
title: Lossy views over an append-only master log with byte-range recovery references embedded in every truncated message
one_why: Compaction never rewrites conversation.jsonl: it forks a view branch and each summary carries the exact byte range of the original, so aggressive compaction stays fully reversible by a tool call - no other subject pairs view branching with byte-level recoverability.

subject: gptme
title: 10% minimum-savings floor before compacting, plus a CACHE_INVALIDATED bus and TTL-based cold-cache prediction
one_why: Nuance vs codex-4: gptme estimates savings BEFORE triggering so a marginal compaction never pays a cache-invalidation penalty, and exposes is_cache_likely_cold() (300s Anthropic TTL heuristic) so plugins trim before a predicted cold request rather than after.

subject: gptme
title: Denylist and sensitive-path re-checks bind before any confirmation, including on user-edited commands
one_why: Nuance vs cline-4/codex-1: not a DSL - a built-in denylist plus sensitive-path prefixes that force confirmation even for allowlisted commands, with is_denylisted re-run on EDIT results so the confirm flow cannot be used to smuggle a denied command past itself.

subject: gptme
title: Deterministic confused-deputy blocker shipping in shadow mode by default with promote-to-enforce via env knob
one_why: Addresses the --no-confirm problem below the model and above the OS, but ships observable-first: shadow logs what would block, enforce blocks, no code change to promote - the rollout pattern is the portable part; note it is NOT enforce by default, so autonomous runs are unprotected unless opted in.

subject: gptme
title: TOFU trust DB hashes the project's hook+context-cmd command set, so editing a project hook re-prompts
one_why: Nuance vs crush-2/pi-4: trust is keyed to a hash of the actual command set, not just the project path - a silently-edited gptme.toml hook loses trust automatically.

subject: gptme
title: Severity-tiered prompt-injection screening of untrusted tool outputs with [UNTRUSTED] context marking
one_why: Screens shell/read/browser/gh/mcp outputs; HIGH patterns get block-mode marking, LOW stays warn-only; default warn and pattern-based (bypassable), but output-marking-into-context converges on something no anchor shipped, and hits persist to injection-attempts.jsonl.

subject: gptme
title: Shipped offline mock provider (mock/echo, mock/static) in the model catalog for no-network loop testing and demos
one_why: Nuance vs pi-8/cline-2/codex-5: the faux provider is a first-class user-facing model spec, not a test harness - CI, demos, and offline dev exercise the real reply() plumbing with zero auth.

subject: gptme
title: Eval quality gate runs 5 real-model evals on every core-path PR and comments a pass-rate report
one_why: Real evals-in-CI exists (the anchors' missing rung) but Phase-1 informational: continue-on-error plus fork PRs skip for lack of API key, so it does not gate merges - still the strongest eval-in-CI artifact in the corpus.

subject: gptme
title: Durable attestation of which model was requested, how aliases resolved, and what evidence exists about the serving backend
one_why: Answers 'was the model I paid for actually the model that served the turn' as a first-class audit artifact per session; nobody else in the corpus tracks provider/checkpoint provenance at all.

subject: gptme
title: Autonomous mode fail-open: no TOOL_CONFIRM hook registered means every tool auto-confirms unless guardrails are explicitly promoted to enforce
evidence: gptme/hooks/confirm.py:228-236 (no-hook auto-confirm), gptme/sandbox.py:117 (GPTME_SANDBOX default none), gptme/hooks/guardrails.py:15-21 (default shadow), injection_screening.py:77 (default warn)
one_why: Individually honest and documented, cumulatively: --no-confirm runs have zero binding protection by default - denylist is the only unconditional layer; the shadow/off defaults put the safe configuration behind four separate env opt-ins.

subject: gptme
title: Durable file-based steering queue with a closed-sentinel protocol whose write-ordering races against concurrent subagent_steer() are explicitly argued in comments
one_why: Mid-run follow-ups land as JSONL with a lock and a sentinel written before the final drain so a steer can never be falsely acknowledged; the belt-and-suspenders reasoning is written down at each break/raise point - a rare example of documented concurrency intent.

subject: gptme
title: Process-scan detection of concurrent rival agents (claude, codex, aider, goose, opencode, amp) sharing the workspace, lock-free by design
one_why: Deliberately avoids lock files (no stale locks on SIGKILL) and reads model/mode/branch from the rival processes themselves - collision-awareness across runtimes is a category no other subject attempts.
